subject: Draw this scene: the cut face of a peat bog, a low wall of dark brown peat with straight spade cuts. Lying curled on his side in the peat is a bog body, a man dead for two thousand years: his skin shrunken, creased and leathery, almost black, pulled tight over the bones; his arms and legs thin as sticks with knobbly joints, his hands bony and claw-like with long thin fingers, his face sunken with closed eyes, a few strands of reddish hair on his head, a corroded green copper band clasped round one thin upper arm. Nothing about him looks alive: he is desiccated and dark like old leather. Wet black peat around him, a fringe of heather and bog grass along the top of the cut, dim grey light. The body lies across the middle of the frame.
